customer_acme: Hey — after we pushed a change to our corporate proxy at 08:15 UTC streaming responses to our Dedicated / Private endpoint are frequently disconnecting mid-event. Client sees partial SSE lines, then reconnects and sometimes gets duplicated payloads (and duplicate billing). Anyone seen this with corp proxies?

laura: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a quick curl that reproduces and which route/model you're calling? Also which proxy vendor/version? :eyes:

customer_acme: Repro curl below. Model route: /v1/streams (text-generation). Proxy is F5 BIG-IP v15, we enabled L7 inspection and HTTP buffering recently.

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N \ 
  "https://private.acme.example/v1/streams?model=rw-small" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"stream test"}'
```

raj: thanks. Two quick suspects: MTU/MSS clamping on the F5 + HTTP buffering re-fragmenting chunk boundaries; or the proxy terminating TLS and doing TCP-level segmentation changes. Do you know your MTU and whether TSO/GSO is enabled on the ingress?

customer_acme: MTU on their edge = 1400 (we're 1500 inside). They enabled HTTP buffer and OFFLOAD settings are default on the F5. Packet trace shows a FIN/RST shortly after ~1460 bytes of data.

ben: can you upload a pcap of a failed session (server->client) captured on the on-prem ingress? `tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w sse-fail.pcap host <client-ip> and port 443` We need to see exact fragmentation and whether SSE event separators (`\n\n` or `data:`) are split across TCP segments.

customer_acme: uploaded pcap to your portal: https://rwd-support/pcap/abc123 (private link). I can repro fairly quickly.

laura: I looked at the pcap — I can see SSE payload being split mid-line by the proxy. The client receives partial event text then the connection resets, client reconnects and requests resume; sometimes the reconnect fetches the remainder and the app processes the second part again => duplicate semantics.

raj: this is a known pattern with proxies that buffer and re-chunk HTTP responses. When they re-emit chunks the original SSE framing can be broken. For Dedicated/Private (on-prem) this gets worse if MTU != 1500 or MSS clamping occurs. Quick workarounds to try: 
- disable proxy response buffering (F5: `http profile` -> disable buffering)
- enable periodic SSE heartbeats from the server (e.g., `: ping\n\n`) every 5s so clients can detect liveness
- set smaller application-side chunk sizes or add `X-Chunk-Size: 512` header to force smaller writes
- try `TCP_NODELAY` on client to avoid Nagle batching

customer_acme: tried `proxy_buffering off` equivalent and set heartbeat at 5s — stream stabilized in our quick test. Any Redwood-side config we should change for Private deployments to be more resilient?

laura: yes — action items for us and guidance for customers: 
1) Docs note: corporate proxies that do L7 reassembly must be configured to not re-chunk or must pass through SSE/TCP with minimal buffering.
2) Recommend setting MTU alignment (1500) between ingress and internal networks or enable MSS clamping to avoid mid-payload fragmentation.
3) We can emit an optional diagnostic header `X-RW-Chunk` showing server chunk boundaries to help customers debug.

raj: for the immediate troubleshooting please provide: 
- the F5 HTTP profile snippet (obfuscate secrets)
- the tcpdump pcap (you uploaded)
- a failing curl log (`-v -N`) output from the client side
We will reproduce in our lab with a simulated F5 config.

customer_acme: attached the snippet and I pasted the verbose curl output to the portal. Quick note: when we flip F5 to TLS passthrough (no L7), stream is stable. So the proxy L7 reassembly looks like root cause.

laura: thanks — that's a very helpful datapoint. I'll open an internal ticket so eng can test with the same F5 options. In the meantime, keep proxy in passthrough if possible or keep `proxy_buffering off`. :thumbsup:

ingress-bot: Ticket SUP-4289 created: "onprem-F5-L7-rechunking-causes-SSE-mid-event-cuts" assigned to raj, priority P2, ETA 48 hours.

ben: one operational note on billing/duplicates — if duplicates are caused by network reconnects and are <1% we can waive those tokens once we validate captures. Please include case id in your support reply.

customer_acme: will monitor for 24h and report back. Thanks everyone, heartbeats + buffer off works for now.

laura: closing loop later — we'll add a short KB on Dedicated/Private SSE gotchas (MTU mismatch, proxy buffering, TLS-termination). If you see reoccurence please paste the new pcap and we'll escalate.
